official.deadline_note: In most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year; the exact date is set by each consortium and published on that master's own website.
official.application_cycle: Annual intake; each master's website publishes its own application deadline
official.status_note: The EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue is live and updated annually, listing the master's programmes currently supported by the EU (218 projects listed at the time of checking). The catalogue notes that some programmes offer no Erasmus Mundus scholarships because they are reaching the end of their funding period or are using the name temporarily after funding.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Programme Guide: 'Selected projects cannot charge student application fees. Moreover, projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders.'

official.application_route: Choose a programme from the EACEA catalogue, then apply directly to that consortium through the programme's own website - there is no central EU application.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students from all over the world; no nationality restriction.
official.international_eligibility: Open to master's-level students from all over the world.

official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are master's degrees jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, plus academic and non-academic associated partners. The European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, maintained by EACEA and updated annually, lists the programmes currently supported by the EU, and scholarships are available for outstanding students at participating programmes.
official.region: Europe (Sweden is one of the catalogue's country filters; the scheme is pan-European and worldwide for students)
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) - jointly designed master's delivered by an international consortium

applicant_utility.summary: There is no central Erasmus Mundus application: you apply to one consortium, for one programme, through that programme's own website, which means each programme is a separate deadline, a separate document set and a separate selection panel. The money is a single published rate - EUR 1,400 per month for the full duration of the programme, up to 24 months - plus coverage of participation costs and travel, visa, installation and subsistence, so tuition cannot be charged to you if you hold the scholarship. Because the EU caps any one nationality at 10% of a consortium's scholarships, students from heavily applied countries face the hardest competition, so apply to more than one programme rather than betting on a single consortium. Read each catalogue entry carefully, since the catalogue itself warns that some listed programmes offer no scholarships because their EU funding has run out and only the name is being used temporarily.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year or recent bachelor's graduates who want a multi-country European master's and can absorb a full-time, application-heavy process between October and January.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist several programmes from the EACEA catalogue and confirm on each programme's own website whether it currently offers Erasmus Mundus scholarships, not just the Erasmus Mundus label
Diarise each consortium's deadline separately - the October-January window is a norm, not a shared cutoff
Check the mobility design: at least two study periods in two countries you have not lived in, each of at least one semester or 30 ECTS
Confirm you will hold your bachelor's degree before the programme starts, since enrolment depends on it
Open the programme's Student Agreement template on its website so you know the obligations before you accept
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the European Commission instead of the consortium, which is never the route
Assuming every catalogue programme still funds scholarships; some are in a temporary name-use period
Being over the 10% nationality cap within a consortium without realising the quota exists
Applying for a programme whose mobility design conflicts with your personal situation
Missing the individual consortium deadline because the only date you tracked was the general October-January window
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Costs beyond the monthly allowance and the participation, travel, visa, installation and subsistence coverage, including anything the consortium charges non-scholarship holders, pre-departure relocation from home, and personal spending.
document_audit: Each programme's website publishes its own document list and its own steps for applying with and without a scholarship - read both, because the scholarship route often adds an evaluation stage
A Student Agreement must be signed with the consortium at enrolment, so review it before committing
The degree can be a joint single diploma or multiple national diplomas - check which one your target programmes award before applying
A reduced scholarship duration applies where prior learning is recognised, but never below one academic year
If you already held an EMJM scholarship you cannot apply for another one under EMJM
alerts: Prior EMJM scholarship holders are excluded from applying again, so first-time applicants only
The scholarship is only paid in full and only to full-time students
Compulsory physical mobility cannot be replaced with virtual or distance learning
Top-up scholarships exist for students from specified world regions funded by other EU instruments, so regional priorities may matter to your ranking
Selected projects cannot charge application fees to students, so any fee demand is a red flag
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Pick a programme from the EACEA catalogue, apply through that programme's own website within its own deadline, and sign the consortium's Student Agreement on enrolment.
